title: This is Frontline RTS, a real-time strategy game I've been developing with AI.
author: guy_ships_things
selftext: I'm building a classic base-building RTS. Here is a 36 v 36 tank and infantry battle with the new combat effects (muzzle flashes, shock rings, burning wrecks)"

comments.author: guy_ships_things
comments.body: If someone want to try it let me know i can send the website, you can try the testing game till i upload it for steam

comments.author: Dizzyeah
comments.body:
Did you pay attention in your trailer that at the bottom right corner, a building flicker in place ?  
You should make your trailer pristine if you want to make people interested. Especially given the "slop" aura that comes with IA games (which is, for low effort content, totally justified IMO, low effort content is akin to an asset flip, but you don't even code it yourself anymore).  
And I don't say that to be super mean (I wouldn't have bothered typing), but as a suggestion on what to improve on your presentation.  
And good luck on your game !

replies.author: guy_ships_things
replies.body:
Thank you... i will do so...
Thanks alot

replies.author: Livid-Evidence579
replies.body: I don't think this is a trailer I think OP was just excited about what he was making and posted a little bit of gameplay

replies.author: Dizzyeah
replies.body:
I believe my point still stands if you want to share publicly something to the world. Especially if your goal is to make people interested.  
If the first thing I see in a short video of a project is an obvious glitch, that does not make me want to engage at all, so that's why, I write it in good faith, not to mock, but to point it out.

comments.author: Livid-Evidence579
comments.body: Does it have any unique gameplay mechanics or aesthetics and you don't have to answer that here for fear of the vultures but if it doesn't I would start thinking about that otherwise I think it looks pretty cool and interesting I was always a huge fan of all the command and conquer games maybe we should trade notes how long have you been developing this

replies.author: guy_ships_things
replies.body: Thanks, glad you like it. I grew up on Command and Conquer too, and that's the feel I'm going for: harvesters, base building, big tank fights. There is one mechanic I think is new for this kind of game, but like you said, I'm keeping that one to myself until it's closer to release. I've been building that secret for about a month now and overallgame about 4 months. Happy to trade notes, what are you working on?

comments.author: niloony
comments.body: You really need to improve unit readability.

replies.author: guy_ships_things
replies.body: Thank you, The tanks blend into the ground and the two sides are hard to tell apart in a big fight. I'm working on it now: stronger team colours and clearer outlines. Was the main problem telling the sides apart, or seeing the units against the terrain?

comments.author: krayon_kylie
comments.body:
this is bad dawg

listen, as a failed musician let me give you one piece of advice i should have taken when i was younger

\*never release your demos\*

replies.author: Livid-Evidence579
replies.body: Well I guess the only thing this post proves is never listen to advice from a failure... Not to be mean to you bro but this guy is actually doing something and putting it out there. What he made may not be perfect but he was bold enough to put it out there. Is there room for improvement sure but as someone who's developing their own game as well I can tell you to even get to this point of Polish takes a long time even with AI.
